subject: STABLE encode-cpu-opus: bridge code-cache compare fix (gate-green 16:11-16:20 on C6q e5486c6); host submit 1.48 us/job + 2.39 us/draw -> 1.31 + 1.46 (-39% per draw); HEAVY RELEASE
body:
GATES
- run_host_tests: all passed, including the iOS strict link.
- CA: PASS. Render: 32. Async: 7/7.
- Integration: only the known CA pass failure.

CHANGE (nord2_metal_bridge.c, claimed functions only)
- cached_code compares against a malloc'd host copy of each cached binary (code_copy[16], freed on eviction, reclaim and close). It compares 8 bytes per step after a first/last-word reject, instead of a byte loop over the cache BO's CPU mapping (GPU memory).
- n2mb_draw_batch_mrt reuses the previous draw's code BO when the shader pointer and length are equal within the call.

MEASURED
- Host, frame_bench fit over 12 scenario/mode rows, C6q bridge vs this:
  - 1.48 us/job + 2.39 us/draw -> 1.31 us/job + 1.46 us/draw.
  - ca200 batched 518 -> 332 us/frame; large 294 -> 187; blur_heavy 159 -> 90.
- Device effect: not measured. It should be at least proportional: no per-draw reads of GPU-mapped memory, and 0.8 MB blur binaries are no longer byte-scanned per draw.

TOOLING
- tools/frame_bench_main.m: FB_PROF=<file> samples the execute phase.
- tools/fb_prof_report.py resolves the samples.

md5: see the reply. Next: the three handed-over hotspots, one at a time.
